source: Robert Louis Stevenson, The Silverado Squatters, Part I, In the Valley, chapter III, Napa Wine (Chatto and Windus, 1883)

evidence.where: Project Gutenberg plain text of The Silverado Squatters (ebook 516, transcribed from the 1906 Chatto and Windus impression), downloaded and grepped this run; the paragraph read around line 514
evidence.edition: The Silverado Squatters, Chatto and Windus, first published 1883; text read in the 1906 impression
evidence.locator: chapter III, Napa Wine, the sentence those virtuous Bonanzas, where the soil has sublimated under sun and stars to something finer, and the wine is bottled poetry: these still lie undiscovered

reason: The words are verbatim, but only as the tail of a relative clause about vineyards that, Stevenson says, still lie undiscovered. Lifted alone with a raised capital, the card turns a prophecy into a maxim, and its fame belongs to the misquote Wine is bottled poetry. It also serves Gratitude and Mortality only thinly. It fails a second time and is out.
